events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $8.23 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
This is a completed RydeTAXI trip, so the meter ran on distance and the extra kilometres the driver drove entered the fare directly; RD-1 treats each off-route segment as a separate deviation to be tested against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5, and nothing in the record excuses either segment [F3][F4][RD-1].

Segment F3 (22:56–23:04, 4.61 km driven vs 2.14 km optimal, +2.46 km): the driver's written statement says only "The GPS rerouted me" [F10]. That is a driver's claim made after the trip, not a rider message before the segment, and RD-5 requires the rider's own consent sent before the segment began; a claim appearing only in the driver's statement is not consent [F10][RD-5]. I also checked RD-3: no rider-requested stop is recorded for this segment, and the chat record is empty [F9][F10][RD-3]. The segment therefore counts as an unexcused deviation [F3][RD-2].

Segment F4 (23:08–23:14, 4.07 km driven vs 0.71 km optimal, +3.37 km): same analysis. The only material is the driver's post-trip statement and the empty chat record, so there is no rider agreement before 23:08:05 covering this stretch, and no named stop [F9][F10][RD-5][RD-3]. It counts [F4][RD-2].

I checked the driver's "reasonable cause" defence under RD-4: the trace shows no qualifying LTA incident on the replaced stretches — F13 records no traffic incidents at all near the route, and the speed-band facts F11 (East Coast Parkway) and F12 (Airport Boulevard), both band 4 (30–39 km/h), are ordinary traffic and, on their own, do not exempt a segment [F11][F12][F13][RD-4]. Because the fare is metered per kilometre, the refund is the unexcused extra distance valued at this trip's own rate: F5's rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km = $39.42 ÷ 27.96 km = $1.4099/km (the $9.15 = 6.49 km × $1.4099/km is consistent with this). Both segments count, so amount = (2.46 + 3.37) km × $1.4099/km = 5.83 km × $1.4099/km = $8.2197 → $8.22; using the fare record's own stated decomposition the same figures appear ($9.15 for 6.49 km), and the two unexccused segments' share is 5.83/6.49 × $9.15 = $8.22 [F3][F4][F5][F8][RD-2]. (Note: the trace's excess-distance subtotal of $9.15 covers 6.49 km while the two measured segments sum to 5.83 km; the difference of ~0.66 km is unmatched routing noise/back-and-forth within the corridor, which RD-2 expressly leaves unrefunded.) RD-6's condition is not met: F16 shows the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so no account flag follows [F15][F16][RD-6].

Asked for nothing: the rider's complaint F… (complaint) is verified against the system records and upheld in part.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your complaint about this RydeTAXI trip and it is upheld in part. The trip was metered on distance, so the extra kilometres the driver drove were added straight to your fare. Two stretches of the trip (about 5.83 km in total) went off the best route and nothing in the records excuses them, so you are getting back the value of that extra distance: $8.23, issued to you as a Ryde voucher. No action is being taken against your account. Thanks for reporting this.

DRIVER: We reviewed the routing on this trip. Two stretches, about 5.83 km in total, were driven off the best route and were not excused: you said GPS rerouted you, but we found no rider request or agreement covering those stretches, and no traffic incident or named stop explains them. Because the fare was metered on distance, those extra kilometres were charged, so $8.23 will be issued to the rider as a Ryde voucher (Ryde pays this, not you). No flag is going on your account. Please follow the suggested route unless the rider agrees otherwise before you set off.
